prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (dedicated-by column), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Gordon B. Hinckley dedicated temples across Europe and Africa from the 1980s to the 2000s. They include Freiberg Germany, Stockholm Sweden and Johannesburg South Africa (1985), Preston England (1998), Madrid Spain (1999), The Hague (2002), Copenhagen and Accra Ghana (2004), Aba Nigeria (2005) and Helsinki Finland (2006). He also rededicated London and Bern in 1992.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country where a king of Assyria, Babylon or Egypt ruled or fought, in the Old Testament.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country where a king of Assyria, Babylon or Egypt ruled or fought, in the Old Testament
prompts.note: Places in the West Bank or Gaza, such as Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho or Gaza city, count as Palestine, which is not an answer.
prompts.summary: In the later Old Testament period, Assyria, Babylon and Egypt fought over the lands around Israel. Sennacherib of Assyria besieged Lachish, Pharaoh Necho killed King Josiah at Megiddo, and Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon defeated Necho at Carchemish (Jeremiah 46:2). Nebuchadnezzar also laid a long siege to Tyre and judged King Zedekiah of Judah at Riblah in Syria (2 Kings 25:6).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Nebuchadnezzar ruled from Babylon (Daniel 4:30).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Sennacherib besieged Lachish, and Necho killed Josiah at Megiddo (2 Kings 18:14; 23:29).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Necho was king of Egypt, and Nahum recalls Assyria's sack of No-Amon, Egyptian Thebes (Nahum 3:8).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Ezekiel describes Nebuchadnezzar's long siege of Tyre (Ezekiel 26:7; 29:18).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Tiglath-pileser took Damascus, and Nebuchadnezzar judged Zedekiah at Riblah (2 Kings 16:9; 25:6).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Nebuchadnezzar beat Necho at Carchemish, on the Turkish side of the border (Jeremiah 46:2; Isaiah 10:9).

prompts.summary: Acts names several women in the early Church. Tabitha lived at Joppa, Lydia, who came from Thyatira, hosted Paul at Philippi, and Damaris believed at Athens. Priscilla and her husband Aquila had left Rome when Claudius expelled the Jews (Acts 18:2) and later lived at Ephesus.
